Create a Suitable Financing Route for Solar Customers

Thematic Area: Solar Adoption & Customer Finance

How might we help suitable customers finance a solar-system purchase through a locally available and commercially viable financing arrangement?

Background

An Indonesian solar EPC business has expressed interest in financing and joint ventures. The opportunity is to develop customer purchase financing alongside the separate funding of company-owned energy-service assets.

The objective is to offer suitable customers a clear financing route for a solar-system purchase. Relevant partners provide solar loans, instalment arrangements, credit assessment and EPC-linked finance workflows.

The collaboration will define a customer segment, system sizes, asset ownership and a locally available financing structure with clear payment terms.

Significance of Problem

Without an effective solution, the challenges include:

  • Upfront purchase barriers: A suitable payment route helps customers manage the upfront cost of a solar-system purchase.
  • Difficult purchase comparisons: Inconsistent financing assumptions make total costs and repayment obligations harder to compare.
  • Poor product fit: Financing structures must match local customers, system sizes and repayment requirements.

Existing Efforts

  • Business direction: Financing and joint ventures are part of the company’s stated development interests.
  • Available partner capability: A Vietnam-focused clean-energy finance provider connects financed purchases with EPC partners and supports installation safeguards and repayment administration.
  • Collaboration focus: Develop an Indonesian financing route for a selected customer segment, drawing on relevant financing experience. Define eligibility, ownership, installation acceptance and total payment terms. Separate the EPC business’s system, installation and service revenue from repayments and interest governed by the financing contract.

Potential Market Size

  • Local solar sector: Indonesia reported 916.99 MW of installed rooftop solar in April 2026, indicating an established local market for solar installations and related services.
  • Capital-intensive market: Global solar-project investment is estimated at US$365 billion in 2026, highlighting the sector’s substantial capital requirements.

Eligibility / Qualification

  • Technology readiness: Minimum technology readiness level 3 (TRL3).
  • NUS linkage: NUS student or graduate founder, or incubation through an NUS programme such as BLOCK71.
  • Local and overseas startups: Open to Indonesian and overseas startups.
  • Commitment: Complete the selection process and travel to Indonesia if selected.
